stress noun

mental strain

also stressed, stressful, under stress, stressed out, strain, tension, anguish

classical

Cic. de Or. 2.21, against relaxātiō (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Cael. 39
M-O s.v. stress: nimia vīrium contentiō (Egger)
Traupman 158

contentiō animī

strain, the straining of the mind

Contentiō is a stretching, an exertion of body or mind; Cicero sets it against relaxātiō and remissiō, rest. Too much of it is stress: Egger’s nimia vīrium contentiō. Its other common senses are a contest or dispute, and a comparison. Stressed is sollicitus (worried) or occupātissimus (swamped); stressful, molestus or labōriōsus.

Other words

  • sollicitūdō, sollicitūdinis f. — anxiety, worry

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 5.21.3

    Where the stress is worry (see concern).

  • angor, angōris m. — anguish, a tight-chested distress

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.18: angor est aegritūdō premēns; 4.27 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 149

    Properly a choking; a passing feeling, where anxietās is a lasting state (Cic. Tusc. 4.27).

  • occupātiō, occupātiōnis f. — business, pressure of work (mostly plural)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 12.30.2: maximīs occupātiōnibus distinēbar (Lewis & Short)

    For the stress of having too much to do.

Examples

  • sed dīcēs mē ipsum mihi sollicitūdinem struere.

    but you will say I am making stress for myself.Cic. Att. 5.21.3

  • remōtum ā sollicitūdinibus et cūrīs et necessitāte cotīdiē aliquid contrā animum faciendī

    far from worries and cares and the need to do something against one’s inclination every dayTac. Dial. 13.5

  • omnemque vītae suae cursum in labōre corporis atque in animī contentiōne cōnficeret

    and spent his whole life in physical toil and mental strainCic. Cael. 39

See also concern, pressure, tired, rest, calm down.
